Prevention: Crop rotation for at least one season with crops which are not in the same family with tree tomato such as maize, wheat beans, etc.
Field sanitation to destroy weeds which may act as refuge and alternative hosts for whiteflies.
Where possible, protect seedlings from infection by growing them under 60 mesh screening.
Use physical barriers like hedges to minimize the movement of adult insects from infested field(s) to healthy field (s).
Conserve natural enemies of whitefly such as parasitic wasps (Hymenoptera) in the family
This can be achieved by reducing chemical sprays. keep recently received plants isolated to monitor and prevent the spread any potential infestation
Monitoring: Thoroughly inspect plants before planting for all stages of the pest, particularly on the lower leaves where immature stages are likely to be most visible.
Adult whiteflies are usually found on young leaves.
Monitor throughout the growing season with yellow sticky traps fixed inside or around the field.

Check for the presence of whiteflies by tapping on plants to encourage flight by adults and inspect the leaves for immature “stage” Begin treatment immediately if any of the life stages of the pest are detected to ensure prompt eradication.
Direct Control: Apply soap and oil when whiteflies are resting (early morning or late evening).
Combine 2 table spoons of dishwashing liquid soap and 2 table spoons of vegetable cooking oil with 4 litres of water.
Spray the plant once a week until whiteflies are no longer seen on the plant.
Spray water underside of the leaf to kill adults and reduce the number of eggs.
Restrictions: Spray early morning or late in the evening.
Wear protective clothing when applying pesticides.
Do not harvest within 14 days of applying pesticides.
